chunks: 3877 - And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:
"Whoever plants a tree initially, or digs a valley to which no one had preceded him, or revives dead land, then it belongs to him as a decree from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger."

key_terms.أَحْيَا: revived by developing and making productive
key_terms.أَرْضًا مَيْتَةً: dead land; uncultivated and unused land
key_terms.غَرَسَ: planted or set in the ground
key_terms.قَضَاءً: a binding decree or legal determination

ai.seo_question: Does reviving dead land make it legally belong to the one who develops it in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that a person gains entitlement to unused land or resources through productive initiative, such as planting, digging, or reviving barren land. It reflects a legal principle in Islamic jurisprudence that labor and cultivation can establish rightful possession by the decree of Allah عزّ وجلّ and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3877 - The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said:

"Whoever plants a tree from the beginning, or digs a valley that no one has preceded him in, or revives dead land, then it belongs to him, this is a decree from Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, and His Messenger."
